chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from 'Ali ibn Muhammad, from 'Abd Allah ibn Ishaq, from one whom he mentioned, from Muqatil ibn Muqatil, who said:

I asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about salat (prayer) in al-sammūr, al-sinjāb, and fox furs. He said: There is no good in all of that except for al-sinjāb, for it is a creature that does not eat meat.

key_terms.الثَّعَالِبِ: foxes, whose fur is included in the ruling
key_terms.السَّمُّورِ: sable, a type of fur mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.السِّنْجَابِ: squirrel, the fur excepted from the general disapproval
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual worship whose validity is being discussed
key_terms.اللَّحْمَ: meat, mentioned as the basis for distinguishing the animal
key_terms.دَابَّةٌ: a creature or animal, used here to describe the squirrel
key_terms.لَا خَيْرَ: there is no good, indicating disapproval or invalidity in context

ai.seo_question: Is salat (prayer) permissible in sable, squirrel, or fox fur according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning salat (prayer) in garments made from certain animal furs. Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام disapproves of prayer in all those mentioned except squirrel fur, explaining the exception by its being from a non-carnivorous animal.
